conventions.convention: Cartan–Eilenberg data are a supplied bicomplex in the commuting convention: h and v commute, h^2=v^2=0, the bicomplex is zero for p<b or q<0, the augmentation satisfies h·ε=ε·d_K and v·ε=0, the induced vertical complexes are injective resolutions of K^p, Z^pK, B^pK, H^pK, and the two bidegree-wise sequences 0→B^{p,q}→Z^{p,q}→H^{p,q}→0 and 0→Z^{p,q}→I^{p,q}→B^{p+1,q}→0 are required split exact (splittings not distinguished data); Tot^n I = ⊕_{p+q=n} I^{p,q} carries D = h + (−1)^p v, and the definition makes no existence or choice claim.

Derived objects are relative to supplied resolution data: ℝ_I^n F(K) = H^n(Tot(FI)) keeps the subscript I until independence is proved, no global choice of resolutions for all complexes is asserted, and G-acyclicity is likewise relative to supplied data and imposes no vanishing on G(X)=R^0G(X) (it is not exactness of a complex).

Choice bookkeeping: DC (or the countably many splittings, comparisons and homotopies supplied as data) is assumed for the Cartan–Eilenberg existence, hyperderived independence and the Grothendieck/LHS constructions, always as countable per-construction choices in the ambient-set convention and never as a simultaneous choice over a proper class; AC is used for the PID and vector-space results (complements, free submodules, basis-based sections). Statements record which is used, and no item claims DC or AC is necessary.

Cohomological bidegree convention of the two double-complex sequences: vertical-first has E_1^{p,q}=R^qF(K^p) (p = complex degree, q = resolution degree, p≥b) and horizontal-first has E_2^{p,q}=R^pF(H^qK) (p = resolution degree, q = complex degree, q≥b); in both d_r: E_r^{p,q} → E_r^{p+r,q−r+1}, the abutment filtration is by the printed first index, and translating a lower bound keeps the original total degree p+q.

Convergence and filtration conventions: cohomological items use a finite decreasing filtration normalized by F^0H^n=H^n and F^{n+1}H^n=0 with gr^p H^n = E_∞^{p,n−p}; the homological Künneth/hyper-Tor items use a finite increasing filtration with F_{−1}H_n=0 and F_nH_n=H_n; collapse at E^s means every differential vanishes in every bidegree for all r≥s, and a written double arrow is not by itself a convergence proof.

Edge maps are the composites through the extreme graded pieces of the finite abutment filtration — the augmentation/bottom-cycle inclusion into the target and the projection onto the left axis (first sequence) or resolution degree zero (second sequence); no splitting, monicity or epimorphy is asserted beyond those filtration maps, and transgression in the group-cohomology five-term sequence is d_2^{0,1} with the LHS cochain sign.

Sign and Hom conventions: tensor totals use the Koszul differential d(u⊗v)=du⊗v+(−1)^{|u|}u⊗dv; the Hom cochain complex of a chain complex is Hom(C,M)^n=Hom(C_n,M) with δf=f∘d_C; 'Ext of complexes' means cohomology of derived Hom; the commuting Cartan–Eilenberg total is h+(−1)^p v while the library's homological double complexes are anticommuting with total h+v.

A spectral-sequence computation record must separate page computation, later differentials (including incoming arrows), convergence for the actual filtration, extension/reconstruction and canonical edges, must distinguish existence, choice and naturality of a splitting, and must record the exact use of any choice axiom or the supplied-data alternative; an uncomputed entry is not zero.

The fs- items are refutations: the text under 'Statement' is the false claim under attack and the asserted content of the item is its 'Refutation' section, which must supply an explicit witness; the cex- item likewise states the refuted claim under 'Statement refuted'.

load_bearing.statement: Let F:A→B and G:B→C be additive left-exact functors between abelian categories, with enough injectives in A and B. Suppose F carries injectives to G-acyclic objects. With supplied injective and Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions and compatible comparison data, there is a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}=R^pG(R^qF(A)) ⟹ R^{p+q}(GF)(A).

A Cartan–Eilenberg injective resolution is a bicomplex I, zero for p<b or q<0, with commuting arrows h:I^{p,q}→I^{p+1,q}, v:I^{p,q}→I^{p,q+1}, h^2=v^2=0, hv=vh, an augmentation ε:K→I^{·,0} with hε=εd_K, vε=0, vertical injective resolutions of K^p, Z^pK, B^pK, H^pK, and the two sequences 0→B^{p,q}→Z^{p,q}→H^{p,q}→0 and 0→Z^{p,q}→I^{p,q}→B^{p+1,q}→0 split exact in each bidegree; Tot^n I=⊕_{p+q=n}I^{p,q} with D=h+(−1)^p v.

Let f:K→L be a map of bounded-below complexes and I,J supplied Cartan–Eilenberg injective resolutions, in the commuting convention. Assume DC or supply the countable splittings and extensions used below. There is a bicomplex map a:I→J over f; any two such maps a,a' differ by v_Js+sv_I for maps s^{p,q}:I^{p,q}→J^{p,q−1} commuting with h. After any additive functor, comparisons induce the same maps on vertical-first spectral sequences from E_1, and on horizontal-first spectral sequences from E_2.

Let C^{a,b} be a commuting double cochain complex in an abelian category, zero for a<0 or b<0. Put T^n=⊕_{a+b=n}C^{a,b} with D=h+(−1)^a v. The decreasing filtrations by a≥p and by b≥p give spectral sequences with 'E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C^{p,·}) and ''E_1^{p,q}=H^q(C^{·,p}), both with d_r:E_r^{p,q}→E_r^{p+r,q−r+1} and stationary terms F^pH^{p+q}(T)/F^{p+1}H^{p+q}(T), the filtration finite with F^0H^n=H^n and F^{n+1}H^n=0.

For F additive and left exact and a bounded-below complex K with supplied Cartan–Eilenberg resolution I, ℝ_I^nF(K)=H^n(Tot(FI)), (FI)^{p,q}=F(I^{p,q}), D=F(h)+(−1)^pF(v); without comparison data the subscript I is retained, since the definition alone asserts neither independence nor a choice of a resolution for every complex.

In the setting and comparison-data conventions of the two hypercohomology spectral sequences, the first sequence has canonical edge maps H^n(FK)→ℝ^nF(K)→ker(R^{n−b}F(K^b)→R^{n−b}F(K^{b+1})), and the second has canonical edge maps R^{n−b}F(H^bK)→ℝ^nF(K)→F(H^nK). No map is asserted to split, be monic, or be epic beyond the associated filtration maps.

For the supplied composite data A→I, F(I)→J under the acyclicity and comparison hypotheses of the total-composite lemma, the vertical-first filtration of Tot(GJ) collapses to R^n(GF)(A); the other filtration has E_2^{p,q}=R^pG(R^qF(A)), and its two edges are the canonical maps R^nG(F(A))→R^n(GF)(A) and R^n(GF)(A)→G(R^nF(A)).

Assume DC and supplied resolution data. For an extension 1→N→G→Q→1 and a left G-module M there is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence E_2^{p,q}=H^p(Q,H^q(N,M)) ⟹ H^{p+q}(G,M) with d_r:(p,q)↦(p+r,q−r+1), the abutment having a finite decreasing filtration F^0H^n=H^n, F^{n+1}H^n=0 and graded pieces E_∞^{p,n−p}.

Let C be a bounded-below complex of right R-modules and D a bounded-below complex of left R-modules, and suppose at least one is degreewise flat. With projective Cartan–Eilenberg resolutions of both, E^2_{p,q}=⊕_{i+j=q}Tor^R_p(H_iC,H_jD) ⟹ H_{p+q}(Tot(C⊗_R D)), with d_r of degree (−r,r−1) and a finite increasing filtration by resolution degree; if the lower bounds are c,d the support is p≥0, q≥c+d and all sums in fixed bidegree are finite.

Let C be a bounded-below chain complex of projective left R-modules, M a left R-module, and supply projective Cartan–Eilenberg data for C. Then E_2^{p,q}=Ext_R^p(H_qC,M) ⟹ H^{p+q}(Hom_R(C,M)) is strongly convergent with a finite decreasing filtration by resolution degree, and the page differential has degree (r,1−r).

Assume AC. For bounded-below free complexes C,D over a PID R, the Künneth spectral sequence has only columns p=0,1 and gives the natural short exact sequence 0→⊕_{i+j=n}H_iC⊗_R H_jD→H_n(C⊗_R D)→⊕_{i+j=n−1}Tor_1^R(H_iC,H_jD)→0. It admits splittings, but no splitting natural in both complexes exists in general.

A spectral-sequence computation record specifies input/indexing/support/target conventions with any choice axiom and its exact use or the supplied-data alternative, a computed page with the maps identifying entries (an uncomputed entry is not zero), every later differential in the claimed range including incoming arrows, a convergence proof for the actual filtration, the finite filtration with endpoints and extension problems (distinguishing existence, chosen and natural splittings), and the canonical edge maps with naturality; it is complete in its declared range when no such obligation remains unresolved, and a written double arrow is notation for a convergence assertion, not its proof.

A bounded-below complex K in an abelian category with enough injectives has a Cartan–Eilenberg injective resolution relative to supplied compatible successive choices of embeddings and horseshoe lifts; DC supplies such a sequence when the admissible finite construction data form a set with the serial extension relation described, and no global choice of resolutions for all complexes is asserted.

Let F:A→B and G:B→C be additive left-exact functors, with enough injectives in A,B, and suppose F sends injectives to G-acyclic objects. Supply A→I and a Cartan–Eilenberg resolution F(I)→J. Then the augmentation GF(I)→Tot(GJ) is a quasi-isomorphism, and consequently H^n(Tot(GJ))=R^n(GF)(A) via this canonical comparison.

concerns.concern: Step 2.1 (supplied-data branch) invokes [F3] = thm-horseshoe-lemma-for-injective-resolutions, whose published statement begins 'Assume the Axiom of Dependent Choice. ... Then there exists an injective resolution of A whose degree-n term is a finite product, equivalently biproduct, I'^n⊕I''^n.' The item brackets this with 'its use is the same finite recursive horseshoe construction, without invoking its DC existence assertion', but that separation is nowhere in the cited statement: a reader must verify that degreewise split exactness of the horseshoe sequence and injectivity of the biproduct middle terms are available in ZF once the lifts are supplied. The DC accounting in step 4.1 is otherwise explicit.

Step 3.1 compresses the acyclicity argument for U/F^mU: the successive quotients of the finite column filtration are the individual augmented columns of U with their total degrees shifted, and the induction applying the long exact sequence (plus F^mU being zero in degrees n−1,n,n+1 once m>n+2) is left to the reader. The identification U^n = T^n ⊕ K^{n+1} with Cone(e)^n is likewise stated only up to an explicit sign twist of the K^{n+1} summand, so the sign verification in step 4.1 must be redone by the reader.

F1 and F6 obtain the projective Cartan–Eilenberg data by citing the injective definition and the comparison lemma 'reversed', and step 1.1 fixes the anticommuting form through ṽ_P=(−1)^i v_P, ṽ_Q=(−1)^j v_Q. The dualisation of the split-horizontal-exactness clauses, of the lower bound c,d and of the comparison homotopies to the projective/homological side is asserted rather than displayed, so the first-page computation rests on an index-and-sign dictionary the reader must reconstruct.

Step 2.1 identifies the Q-action on H^1(N,M) computed from the cyclic N-resolution with the action used by LHS's resolution convention, via 'the Hom-to-injective-total comparison in F4 commutes with these actions and its augmentation'; the rank-one transgression claim depends on the Q-fixedness of [b],[d] being the same in both pictures, and F4's statement only asserts the Ext isomorphism/naturality. The direct computation (Sb=c is a T-boundary, Sd=0) is displayed, but the compatibility of the two Q-actions is argued in one sentence.
